manchete.resumo: Nari Ward builds a ship for a port   For the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, Jamaican-American artist Nari Ward has created a giant, land-bound vessel, titled Ground Break Duty, that looks out onto the historical…
manchete.trecho: Nari Ward builds a ship for a port   For the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, Jamaican-American artist Nari Ward has created a giant, land-bound vessel, titled Ground Break Duty, that looks out onto the historical Mina Zayed port , or MiZa for short. Measuring 30 × 30 meters and sitting atop an 18-square-meter copper platform, the skeleton of this purple barge, tipped at an angle, recalls the ‘dhow’ , or a traditional wooden sailing vessel that carries heavy goods around the Gulf and Indian Ocean. noticias.titulo: Timber grid and external stair offer "a wink" to Centre Pompidou at its annexe in Massy
noticias.resumo: French architecture studio PCA-Stream has completed Centre Pompidou Francilien in Massy, a storage and exhibition space fronted by a gridded timber deck and external stair that echo the high-tech character of the iconic…
noticias.trecho: French architecture studio PCA-Stream has completed Centre Pompidou Francilien in Massy, a storage and exhibition space fronted by a gridded timber deck and external stair that echo the high-tech character of the iconic original Centre Pompidou in Paris. Officially named Centre Pompidou Francilien Fabrique de l'Art (Art Factory), the 30,000-square-metre building is the first Centre Pompidou annexe in Île-de-France. It is scheduled to open to the public in spring 2027. Photographs Previous Next Photographs Close Overlooking a small lake, the building will house over 150,000 pieces from the Centre Pompidou's reserve collections made visible to the public through temporary exhibition spaces, alongside private conservation and restoration areas. noticias.titulo: The New York Times Bans Photoshop 2027 for Freelancers – Hidden AI Could Mark Real Photos as AI-Generated
noticias.resumo: The New York Times has told its freelance photographers not to use Adobe Photoshop 2027 (version 28.0.0 and later) on assignments for the paper. According to the email, some functions in the new release use generative…
noticias.trecho: The New York Times has told its freelance photographers not to use Adobe Photoshop 2027 (version 28.0.0 and later) on assignments for the paper. According to the email, some functions in the new release use generative AI in ways that are not apparent to users, and that use can add metadata that identifies a photo as AI-generated. The paper confirmed the rule, Adobe has not commented yet, and I think the real problem sits in how Adobe labels its own tools. The email reached freelancers earlier this week and became public when Threads user nolen_strals posted a screenshot of it, which a freelancer had shared with them. It is signed by Meaghan Looram and Nakyung Han of the Times’ photo department. The key sentence reads: “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for…

noticias.resumo: Portsmouth’s August bank holiday festival had a bit of a problem. Too many people were buying a ticket for one act on one day, then disappearing. Wildish & Co.’s solution is an identity that puts the city first. Who…
noticias.trecho: Portsmouth’s August bank holiday festival had a bit of a problem. Too many people were buying a ticket for one act on one day, then disappearing. Wildish & Co.’s solution is an identity that puts the city first. Who doesn’t love a good festival? I’ve been to my fair share over the last thirty years, and I can always tell you which bands were playing. The Prodigy in 1995 and Bowie in 2000, both at Glastonbury. Cypress Hill at V Festival in 2022 along with Asian Dub Foundation, I think it was. Björk at Bluedot a few years ago. Fun times. If you’re running an event like this, you’ll know a lot hangs on your line-up. If it isn’t good enough, people simply won’t book. Victorious Festival knows this only too well. It’s all fun and games until Zoe starts using her camera during an intimate moment, leaving Keira unsure how to feel about it. Directed by Thai architect and designer Kulapat Yantrasast, the exhibition will delve into the city’s historic role as a major Silk Road gateway, further drawing on Uzbek hospitality culture, which is rooted in reciprocity.  The biennial will feature a balanced selection of international and homegrown practitioners. bolhas.titulo: New Currents: Liu Bin’s Luminous Mycologies
bolhas.resumo: Elasticity is governed by time and touch; it lives in the beat between prod and rebound, which makes it a hard quality to capture in a painting. Liu Bin achieves this feat. In his tableaux, mushrooms rise in regal…
bolhas.trecho: Elasticity is governed by time and touch; it lives in the beat between prod and rebound, which makes it a hard quality to capture in a painting. Liu Bin achieves this feat. In his tableaux, mushrooms rise in regal ensembles, their turgid forms resilient, rubbery, resplendent. Exquisite and alive, their ribbed gills and sinewy skins communicate a mute, surreptitious vitality, each cap rendered with a jewel-like precision that borders on the predatory. Liu’s magical realism does not offer an escape from reality but a celebration of its most elegant horrors. Liu Bin, a native of Heilongjiang, China’s northern frontier with Russia, is drawn to an organism most at home in the margins. Mushrooms thrive in the shadows: some gorge on the dead, others prey on living hosts, or trade with the roots of trees. Their particular allure, and repulsiveness, lie in an invertebrate fleshiness alien to the…
